findings.title: Recovery-code metadata is discarded when writing to user storage
findings.body: The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel contains the generated-at timestamp and user label, but the UserCredentialModel sent to user storage contains only the type and a JSON array of raw codes. A user-storage provider has no way to recover the original timestamp or label from this input. Consequently, externally stored recovery-code credentials cannot preserve the same credential metadata as locally stored ones (the added test provider already substitutes the save time and returns a null label), affecting credential/account metadata and audit consistency.

findings.title: Returned recovery-code credentials do not retain their persisted ID
findings.body: updateCredential assigns an ID to myUser.recoveryCodes, but getCredentials reconstructs a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with createFromValues and never copies that persisted ID. The model returned to Keycloak therefore has no ID, or an ID unrelated to the stored record. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator uses the returned ID when all codes are exhausted and calls removeStoredCredentialById, so the external credential cannot be reliably removed; account credential operations also cannot address the actual stored recovery credential.

findings.title: The user-storage recovery validator leaves accepted codes reusable
findings.body: The recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the stored JSON list and never removes or marks that value as used. Every successful recovery code can therefore be submitted repeatedly, and the all-codes-used path is never reached. Recovery codes are required to be one-time credentials; the newly added integration test authenticates only once, so it passes while failing to exercise this essential behavior. The storage fixture should persist consumption (and remove the credential after the final code), with a test proving that a reused code is rejected.
